answer: An agent registers by locking a deposit vesting over thirty epochs as a slashable bond, putting its own money behind the name. The fault is proven by the challenge clock when an agent is caught missing three straight epoch challenges. Once the fault is proven, the slashed funds flow into the insurance pool. Registration demands a ferrous bond: a fake costs real money from day one. The network watches every mirror for a second identity on the same funds. The sable bond is the price of admission, and farms pay it per fake.
